header.title: Software Development Engineer III, Java
header.lead: A hard senior role, deliberately. Java-first, full-stack when the work needs it. You'll own a domain end to end, make the calls without waiting to be told, and answer for them in production.
header.punchline: We hold this bar and we don't lower it to fill the seat.

the_role.lead: We're hiring a small number of senior engineers who can be handed a business problem and come back with a shipped system.
paragraphs: You'll own a domain — claims, wallet, subscriptions, provider network or payments — and be the person accountable for it. Not just the code: the design, the release, the failures, the cost, and the next engineer who has to change it.

Java and Spring Boot are the centre of gravity, but the boundary of your work is the feature, not the language. Expect to write Node services, ship React screens, run your own Kubernetes deployments and debug your own Kafka consumers rather than filing a ticket and waiting.

The problems arrive unfinished. Insurance partners, regulators, hospitals and finance teams each constrain how a feature has to behave, they don't agree with each other, and a member is relying on the result during a hospital visit. Your job is to turn that into a plan, defend the plan in review, ship it, and keep it standing.

We're small enough that your work is live within days, and consequential enough that a rushed decision is paid for by a dozen engineers and thousands of members. We hire at this level to get both halves right.

the_level.lead: Not years, not lines of code. These six are what the level actually asks you to carry.

rows.text: A domain, end to end. You set the design and defend it.
The problem arrives as a business goal. You turn it into a plan.
Your team's technical direction, and the teams that depend on you.
You make the hard trade-offs and own how they turn out.
You're the last line of defence. If it breaks in production, it's yours.
The team ships better because you're on it.

groups.label: DESIGN
bullets: Own the **HLD** — service boundaries, data flow, scale, failure modes, and the trade-offs written down where someone can argue with them.
Own the **LLD** — schemas, class and API contracts, state transitions, concurrency, and the edge cases everyone else discovers in production.
Take both through review before you build. Design that only exists in your head isn't a design.

groups.label: BUILD
bullets: Design, build, test and maintain Java services — clean, readable, and documented well enough that someone else can take them over.
Own the APIs other teams depend on, and keep them stable while the product underneath keeps changing.
Get money and health data right the first time: correct, traceable, and safe to retry when something fails halfway.
Make data-model decisions you can live with, and change them safely once real members are on them.

groups.label: RUN
bullets: Carry your services in production. You'll know something is wrong before a customer tells us.
Instrument before you ship — dashboards, alerts and error budgets are part of the feature, not a follow-up ticket.
Debug the hard ones — the slow, the intermittent, the ones that only happen at month-end — and fix the cause, not the symptom.
Keep things fast and cost-sensible, and back every claim about it with numbers.
Treat member data as confidential by default. Privacy and security aren't a separate checklist here.

groups.label: MULTIPLY
bullets: Set technical direction for your domain, and write the short docs that make a decision reviewable a year later.
Review code quickly and usefully — aimed at what will actually hurt later, not at style.
Mentor engineers, unblock them, and leave the team's default quality higher than you found it.
Say no with a reason. Push back on scope, on timelines and on your own earlier decisions when the evidence changes.

the_bar.intro: Skills get you the interview. These get you the offer, and they're the things we won't compromise on.

traits.title: High ownership
traits.text: You treat the systems you build as your own and drive them from idea to production to long-term upkeep. You instrument them, you watch them, you get paged for them. No handing it over at the merge commit.

traits.title: Highly motivated and self-driven
traits.text: A bias toward action and a strong sense of accountability. You find the next most useful thing to do without being assigned it, and you say clearly when something slips.

traits.title: Extensive AI use
traits.text: You already use Copilot, Claude or ChatGPT heavily — development, code review, debugging, documentation — and you still read every line you ship, because you're the one accountable for it.

traits.title: Fast, with a floor under it
traits.text: You ship in days, not quarters, and you don't buy that speed by skipping tests or leaving the mess for the next person.

traits.title: Direct and low-ego
traits.text: You disagree in the design review, not in the retro. You change your mind when someone is right, and you write things down so the team doesn't have to keep asking you.

ai.lead: AI-assisted development is the default here, not a novelty. We expect it to show up in what you get done.
bullets: Use Copilot, Claude or ChatGPT extensively and daily — scaffolding, tests, refactors, code review, debugging, documentation, migrations.
Read and own every line you ship. "The AI wrote it" is not an explanation for a production incident.
Know where it's weak — unfamiliar domain rules, security-sensitive paths, and anything touching money or member health data. Verify those yourself.
Build the workflow, not just the habit: the prompts, context and repo conventions that make the whole team faster, not only you.
Have opinions about AI in the product too, not only in the toolchain. We're building it into what members use.

items: **6+ years** of professional software development, the majority of it in Java — depth, not the same year repeated.
**Strong Java** (8 or higher; 17+ preferred) and real Spring / Spring Boot experience, not tutorial-level familiarity.
**Production Node.js** — services you built and ran, not scripts.
**Working React** — you can carry a feature from API to UI without waiting for someone else.
**System design at both altitudes** — HLD you can defend in a review, and LLD detailed enough to hand to another engineer.
**Kafka** or similar event-driven systems, run in production rather than prototyped.
**Kubernetes and containers** — you deploy, debug and scale your own service.
**Good database judgement** across SQL (MySQL, PostgreSQL) and MongoDB — you can find a slow query and fix it yourself.
**Observability as a habit** — the metrics, logs, traces, dashboards and alerts on your services were set up by you (Prometheus, Grafana, Sentry, ELK or equivalent).
**Extensive daily AI use** already built into how you work.
Experience **designing, shipping and operating** backend services that real users depend on.
Experience being the **owner and on-call** for something you built.
**Bachelor's degree** in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
**Clear written and spoken communication** in a cross-functional team.
You've led the design of a project that spanned more than one team.
You've measurably improved an existing system — reliability, latency or cost — and can show the before and after.
You've run a production incident end to end and written the postmortem yourself.
Experience mentoring engineers, or informally leading a small team.
TypeScript end to end, and React Native or another mobile surface.
You've built with LLM APIs, not only used AI tooling.
Payments or fintech background — gateways, refunds, reconciliation.
Health insurance domain exposure — cashless approvals, claims, renewals.
Experience handling regulated or sensitive customer data.

rows.value: React web, React Native mobile app
Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT — in the daily workflow

assessment.lead: Six dimensions. We index on judgement and evidence, not on how many technologies you can name.

cards.title: Coding
cards.text: Correct, readable code under time pressure — and the restraint to keep the solution as simple as the problem allows.

cards.title: High-level design
cards.text: A real Onsurity-shaped problem, designed out loud. Boundaries, data flow, scale, failure cases — and what you'd deliberately cut.

cards.title: Low-level design
cards.text: The same problem one level down. Schemas, contracts, state transitions, concurrency, and the edge cases you thought of unprompted.

cards.title: Debugging
cards.text: A production symptom with incomplete information. What you check first, how you narrow it, and how you stop it recurring.

cards.title: Ownership deep-dive
cards.text: One system you owned. We'll go deep — why those decisions, what broke, what it cost, what you'd do differently.

cards.title: Bar and collaboration
cards.text: How you handle disagreement and being wrong, and whether the engineers around you get measurably better.

items: You want a tightly specified ticket queue. Here you'll often write the plan before you write the code.
You need a long ramp before you contribute. We'd expect you shipping meaningfully inside your first few weeks.
You'd rather hand a service off once it's live. Ownership here includes the boring long tail and the 2 a.m. page.
You're uncomfortable working where a bug can delay someone's hospital admission. That's the seriousness this team runs at.
